```{r load data, warning=F, message=T}

print(getwd())
print(here::here())

source(here::here("analysis", "0-config.R"))

library(fuzzyjoin)
library(stringi)
library(units)

max_string_dist <- 0.15    # Jaro-Winkler distance (0-1); higher = more permissive
distance_cutoff_km <- 1    # max distance for two records to count as the same village


mordor_grappe <- rbind(readRDS(here("data", "untouched", "from-mordor", "morb_gps.rds")),
                       readRDS(here("data", "untouched", "from-mordor", "main_gps.rds")))

df_all <- readRDS(here("data","grappe_mortality_data.rds")) %>%
  # mordorstate: TRUE for districts (Boboye, Falmey, Loga) that overlapped
  # with the MORDOR mass azithromycin trial in Niger. Included as a covariate
  # to test whether MORDOR districts have systematically different baseline mortality.
  mutate(mordorstate = ifelse(district %in% c("Boboye", "Falmey", "Loga"), TRUE, FALSE))

# Project coordinates to UTM so distances are in meters, not degrees

df_proj <- df_all %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = global_crs) %>%
  st_transform(crs = proj_crs) %>% # UTM zone 31N, for Niger
  mutate(lon = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,1],
         lat = sf::st_coordinates(.)[,2])


boxgrid <- readRDS(here("data", "boxgrid.rds"))

```

```{r}
#| label: "fuzzy-match-villages-functions"

# clean_village_name()
#
# Normalizes a village name for fuzzy matching: strips accents/diacritics,
# lowercases, drops punctuation, and collapses whitespace.
#
# Arguments:
# - x: character vector of raw village names
#
# Requirements:
# - Packages: stringi, stringr
#
# Returns:
# - character vector of cleaned names, same length as x
clean_village_name <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") %>%
    str_to_lower() %>%
    str_replace_all("[^a-z0-9\\s]", " ") %>%
    str_squish()
}

# match_villages_by_name_and_distance()
#
# Matches two village lists across trials in two stages: first generates all
# candidate name pairs within a maximum string-edit distance, then verifies
# each candidate against the geographic distance between the two villages'
# coordinates, computed in a projected CRS. Returns one row per candidate
# pair rather than silently resolving to a single best guess, so ambiguous
# or borderline cases can be reviewed before being finalized.
#
# Arguments:
# - dat_x, dat_y: data frames, one row per village, each with a name column
#   and lat/lon columns
# - name_x, name_y: unquoted village-name column in dat_x / dat_y
# - lat_x, lon_x, lat_y, lon_y: unquoted latitude/longitude columns (WGS84
#   decimal degrees) in dat_x / dat_y
# - projected_crs: EPSG code (integer) of a projected CRS appropriate to the
#   study area; used only for the distance calculation
# - max_string_dist: max Jaro-Winkler distance (0-1) to keep a name-candidate
#   pair before spatial verification. Default 0.15.
# - distance_cutoff_km: max distance (km) between coordinates for a pair to
#   be considered the same village. Default 1.
#
# Details:
# - Candidate generation casts a wide net on string distance so a genuine
#   match with several character edits isn't excluded before it gets a
#   chance to pass the spatial check.
# - A village with exactly one candidate passing the distance cutoff on both
#   sides is "matched". More than one is "ambiguous". A name-candidate that
#   fails the distance cutoff is flagged separately
#   ("name_candidate_failed_distance") rather than dropped. No candidate at
#   all (from the full outer join) is "unmatched".
#
# Requirements:
# - Packages: dplyr, stringr, fuzzyjoin, sf, units
# - Depends on: clean_village_name()
#
# Returns:
# - A tibble with one row per candidate pair: village_x, village_y,
#   string_dist, distance_km, match_status
match_villages_by_name_and_distance <- function(dat_x, dat_y,
                                                id_x, id_y,
                                                 name_x, name_y,
                                                 lat_x, lon_x, lat_y, lon_y,
                                                 projected_crs,
                                                 max_string_dist = 0.15,
                                                 distance_cutoff_km = 1) {

  if (sf::st_is_longlat(sf::st_crs(projected_crs))) {
    stop("projected_crs is a geographic CRS — distances must be computed in a projected CRS.")
  }

  name_x <- rlang::enquo(name_x); name_y <- rlang::enquo(name_y)
  id_x   <- rlang::enquo(id_x);   id_y   <- rlang::enquo(id_y)
  lat_x  <- rlang::enquo(lat_x);  lon_x  <- rlang::enquo(lon_x)
  lat_y  <- rlang::enquo(lat_y);  lon_y  <- rlang::enquo(lon_y)

  dat_x_prep <- dat_x %>%
    transmute(
      village_x = as.character(!!name_x),
      id_x = as.character(!!id_x),
      lat_x = !!lat_x,
      lon_x = !!lon_x,
      name_clean_x = clean_village_name(as.character(!!name_x))
    )

  dat_y_prep <- dat_y %>%
    transmute(
      village_y = as.character(!!name_y),
      id_y = as.character(!!id_y),
      lat_y = !!lat_y,
      lon_y = !!lon_y,
      name_clean_y = clean_village_name(as.character(!!name_y))
    )

  # Stage 1: fuzzy name candidates. mode = "full" keeps villages with no
  # candidate at all (NA on the other side) rather than dropping them ----
  candidates <- stringdist_join(
    dat_x_prep, dat_y_prep,
    by = c("name_clean_x" = "name_clean_y"),
    method = "jw",
    max_dist = max_string_dist,
    distance_col = "string_dist",
    mode = "full"
  )

  # Stage 2: geographic distance in a projected CRS, only where both sides
  # have coordinates ----
  has_both_coords <- !is.na(candidates$lat_x) & !is.na(candidates$lon_x) &
    !is.na(candidates$lat_y) & !is.na(candidates$lon_y)

  pts_x <- st_as_sf(candidates[has_both_coords, ], coords = c("lon_x", "lat_x"),
                     crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) %>%
    st_transform(projected_crs)

  pts_y <- st_as_sf(candidates[has_both_coords, ], coords = c("lon_y", "lat_y"),
                     crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) %>%
    st_transform(projected_crs)

  candidates$distance_km <- NA_real_
  candidates$distance_km[has_both_coords] <- drop_units(
    set_units(st_distance(pts_x, pts_y, by_element = TRUE), "km")
  )

  candidates <- candidates %>%
    mutate(passes_distance = !is.na(distance_km) & distance_km <= distance_cutoff_km)

  # Resolve match status per village, counting valid candidates from each side ----
  match_counts_x <- candidates %>%
    filter(!is.na(village_x)) %>%
    group_by(id_x) %>%
    summarise(n_valid_x = sum(passes_distance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  match_counts_y <- candidates %>%
    filter(!is.na(village_y)) %>%
    group_by(id_y) %>%
    summarise(n_valid_y = sum(passes_distance, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

  candidates %>%
    left_join(match_counts_x, by = "id_x") %>%
    left_join(match_counts_y, by = "id_y") %>%
    mutate(
      match_status = case_when(
        passes_distance & n_valid_x == 1 & n_valid_y == 1 ~ "matched",
        passes_distance ~ "ambiguous",
        is.na(id_x) | is.na(id_y) ~ "unmatched",
        TRUE ~ "name_candidate_failed_distance"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::select(village_x, village_y, id_x, id_y, string_dist, distance_km, match_status)
}

# resolve_ambiguous_by_name_closeness()
#
# For each AVENIR village with more than one MORDOR village passing the
# distance cutoff ("ambiguous" in match_villages_by_name_and_distance()'s
# output), keeps only the MORDOR village whose cleaned name is closest by
# Jaro-Winkler distance.
#
# Arguments:
# - village_matches: tibble returned by match_villages_by_name_and_distance()
#
# Details:
# - Only acts on rows where match_status == "ambiguous".
# - Resolves per AVENIR village only. If two candidates for the same
#   village_x tie exactly on string_dist, the tie can't be broken this way —
#   those rows come back as still_tied.
# - Resolving each AVENIR village independently doesn't guarantee a clean
#   1:1 result: the same MORDOR village can end up as the closest-name pick
#   for more than one AVENIR village. Those cases are flagged in
#   residual_many_to_one rather than silently deduplicated.
#
# Requirements:
# - Packages: dplyr
#
# Returns:
# - A list with three tibbles: resolved, still_tied, residual_many_to_one
#   (same columns as the input, minus match_status)
resolve_ambiguous_by_name_closeness <- function(village_matches) {

  ambiguous <- village_matches %>%
    filter(match_status == "ambiguous")

  if (nrow(ambiguous) == 0) {
    empty <- village_matches[0, ] %>% dplyr::select(-match_status)
    return(list(resolved = empty, still_tied = empty, residual_many_to_one = empty))
  }

  min_dist_per_x <- ambiguous %>%
    group_by(id_x) %>%
    mutate(
      is_min = string_dist == min(string_dist),
      n_min = sum(is_min)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()

  resolved <- min_dist_per_x %>%
    filter(is_min, n_min == 1) %>%
    dplyr::select(-is_min, -n_min, -match_status)

  still_tied <- min_dist_per_x %>%
    filter(is_min, n_min > 1) %>%
    dplyr::select(-is_min, -n_min, -match_status)

  residual_many_to_one <- resolved %>%
    group_by(id_y) %>%
    filter(n() > 1) %>%
    ungroup()

  list(resolved = resolved, still_tied = still_tied, residual_many_to_one = residual_many_to_one)
}

# finalize_village_match_table()
#
# Collapses the candidate table from match_villages_by_name_and_distance(),
# together with the resolved output of resolve_ambiguous_by_name_closeness(),
# into one row per AVENIR village.
#
# Arguments:
# - village_matches: tibble from match_villages_by_name_and_distance()
# - resolved_ambiguous: the `resolved` tibble from
#   resolve_ambiguous_by_name_closeness() — its rows are treated as matched
# - nearest_dist: tibble with one row per AVENIR village, columns village_x
#   and dist_nearest_mordor_km, giving the distance to the nearest MORDOR
#   village regardless of match status
#
# Details:
# - matched is TRUE if the AVENIR village has a "matched" row in
#   village_matches, or a row in resolved_ambiguous. Everything else —
#   "unmatched", "name_candidate_failed_distance", or an ambiguous pair
#   resolve_ambiguous_by_name_closeness() could not resolve (still_tied,
#   residual_many_to_one) — collapses to matched = FALSE. This table does
#   not distinguish among those unresolved cases; go back to
#   village_matches / the resolver's output for that detail.
# - Assumes AVENIR village names are unique; duplicates will collapse.
#
# Requirements:
# - Packages: dplyr
#
# Returns:
# - A tibble with one row per AVENIR village: village_x, matched (logical),
#   village_y, string_dist, distance_km, dist_nearest_mordor_km
finalize_village_match_table <- function(village_matches, resolved_ambiguous, nearest_dist) {

  found <- bind_rows(
    village_matches %>%
      filter(match_status == "matched") %>%
      dplyr::select(village_x, village_y, id_x, id_y, string_dist, distance_km),
    resolved_ambiguous %>%
      dplyr::select(village_x, village_y, id_x, id_y, string_dist, distance_km)
  ) %>%
    mutate(matched = TRUE)

  village_matches %>%
    filter(!is.na(village_x)) %>%
    distinct(id_x, village_x) %>%
    left_join(found, by = c("id_x", "village_x")) %>%
    mutate(matched = coalesce(matched, FALSE)) %>%
    left_join(nearest_dist, by = c("id_x", "village_x")) %>%
    dplyr::select(village_x, id_x, matched, village_y, id_y, string_dist, distance_km, dist_nearest_mordor_km)
}

```

```{r}
#| label: "fuzzy-match-villages"

# Load data -----

avenir_villages <- df_all %>%
  dplyr::select(site_code, village_name = grappe, latitude = lat, longitude = lon)
mordor_villages <- mordor_grappe %>%
  dplyr::select(village_name = grappe, latitude, longitude)
 
# Match -----
 
village_matches <- match_villages_by_name_and_distance(
  dat_x = avenir_villages, dat_y = mordor_villages,
  name_x = village_name, name_y = village_name,
  id_x = site_code, id_y = village_name,
  lat_x = latitude, lon_x = longitude,
  lat_y = latitude, lon_y = longitude,
  projected_crs = proj_crs,
  max_string_dist = max_string_dist,
  distance_cutoff_km = distance_cutoff_km
)

village_matches %>% count(match_status) %>% print(n = Inf)

# Resolve ambiguous pairs by closest name -----
# Check still_tied and residual_many_to_one before trusting the FALSE label
# those villages get in the final table below.

ambiguous_resolution <- resolve_ambiguous_by_name_closeness(village_matches)
# ambiguous_resolution$still_tied
# ambiguous_resolution$residual_many_to_one

# Nearest-MORDOR-village distance for every AVENIR village -----
# Independent of the name match — every AVENIR village gets the distance to
# whichever MORDOR village is geographically closest, in the same projected
# CRS, regardless of whether a name match was found for it.

avenir_pts <- st_as_sf(avenir_villages, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
                        crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) %>%
  st_transform(proj_crs)

mordor_pts <- st_as_sf(mordor_villages, coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
                        crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) %>%
  st_transform(proj_crs)

nearest_mordor_idx <- st_nearest_feature(avenir_pts, mordor_pts)

nearest_dist <- tibble(
  id_x = avenir_villages$site_code,
  village_x = avenir_villages$village_name,
  dist_nearest_mordor_km = drop_units(set_units(
    st_distance(avenir_pts, mordor_pts[nearest_mordor_idx, ], by_element = TRUE), "km"
  ))
)

# Final table -----

final_village_matches <- finalize_village_match_table(
  village_matches, ambiguous_resolution$resolved, nearest_dist
) %>%
  dplyr::select(site_code = id_x, grappe = village_x, 
                match_status = matched, match_mordor_grappe = village_y, match_string_dist = string_dist, match_distance_km = distance_km,
                dist_nearest_mordor_km)

df_all <- df_all %>%
  left_join(final_village_matches, by = c("site_code", "grappe"))

```

## Methods

- We match AVENIR and MORDOR village lists in two stages, since village names in the two source lists frequently differ by spelling, transliteration, or diacritics: fuzzy name matching, followed by spatial distance verification.
- Candidate name pairs are generated using Jaro-Winkler string distance (`method = "jw"`), which tolerates minor spelling variation while remaining sensitive to a shared prefix. Candidates exceeding a string distance of `0.15` are excluded before spatial verification.
- Each surviving candidate is verified against the geographic distance between coordinates, projected to UTM zone 32N (EPSG:32632) rather than computed in geographic coordinates (EPSG:4326). Candidates beyond `1` km are excluded.
- AVENIR villages with exactly one candidate passing both thresholds are matched directly. Villages with more than one passing candidate are resolved to the closest-name candidate where that resolution is unambiguous (no exact string-distance tie, no collision with another AVENIR village's resolved match).
- `site_code` (AVENIR) and `grappe` (MORDOR) serve as primary keys throughout, since village names are not unique within the AVENIR list.
- Distance to the nearest MORDOR village (`dist_nearest_mordor_km`) is computed for every AVENIR village independently of match status, via nearest-feature lookup in the same projected CRS — unmatched villages still carry a meaningful distance rather than a missing value.

## Descriptive statistics

```{r}
district_summary <- df_all %>%
  group_by(district) %>%
  summarise(
    n_villages = n(),
    n_matched = sum(match_status, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_matched = round(100 * n_matched / n_villages, 1),
    median_dist_nearest_mordor_km = round(median(dist_nearest_mordor_km, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
    total_pt_year_1to59 = round(sum(pt_year_1to59, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    total_deaths_1to59 = sum(n_deaths_1to59, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_deaths_per_1000_1to59 = round(median(deaths_per_1000_1to59, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    # assumes isTreated_child's "treated" level is labeled "Treated" —
    # confirm against levels(df_all$isTreated_child) if this looks off
    pct_treated_child = round(100 * mean(isTreated_child == "Treatment", na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(pct_matched))

district_summary %>%
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("District", "N villages", "N matched", "% matched",
                  "Median dist. to nearest MORDOR (km)", "Total person-years (1–59mo)",
                  "Total deaths (1–59mo)", "Median deaths/1000 (1–59mo)", "% treated (child)")
  )
```

- Of `r nrow(df_all)` AVENIR villages, `r sum(df_all$match_status, na.rm = TRUE)`
  (`r round(100 * sum(df_all$match_status, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(df_all), 1)`%) matched
  to a MORDOR village under these thresholds.
- Among matched villages, the median distance between the matched pair is
  `r round(median(df_all$match_distance_km, na.rm = TRUE), 3)` km
  (IQR: `r round(quantile(df_all$match_distance_km, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 3)`–`r round(quantile(df_all$match_distance_km, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 3)` km).
- Across all `r nrow(df_all)` AVENIR villages regardless of match status,
  distance to the nearest MORDOR village has a median of
  `r round(median(df_all$dist_nearest_mordor_km, na.rm = TRUE), 3)` km
  (IQR: `r round(quantile(df_all$dist_nearest_mordor_km, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 3)`–`r round(quantile(df_all$dist_nearest_mordor_km, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 3)` km).
- As expected, match rate varies by district, from
  `r min(district_summary$pct_matched)`% in
  `r district_summary$district[which.min(district_summary$pct_matched)]` to
  `r max(district_summary$pct_matched)`% in
  `r district_summary$district[which.max(district_summary$pct_matched)]`.
- Median distance to the nearest MORDOR village likewise varies by district,
  from `r min(district_summary$median_dist_nearest_mordor_km)` km in
  `r district_summary$district[which.min(district_summary$median_dist_nearest_mordor_km)]`
  to `r max(district_summary$median_dist_nearest_mordor_km)` km in
  `r district_summary$district[which.max(district_summary$median_dist_nearest_mordor_km)]`
  (Table @tbl-district-summary).
- Mortality burden (1–59 months) is comparable between districts with
  higher and lower match rates: median deaths per 1000 person-years ranges
  from `r min(district_summary$median_deaths_per_1000_1to59)` to
  `r max(district_summary$median_deaths_per_1000_1to59)` across districts,
  with no consistent relationship to `pct_matched` — a spot check worth
  revisiting once the `dist_nearest_mordor_km` fix is confirmed, since a
  district-level correlation between match rate and mortality would suggest
  the matching procedure is not missing at random with respect to outcome.

#| label: plot-mordor-village-matches

ggplot(data = df_all, 
       aes(group = district, color = district, 
           x = dist_nearest_mordor_km, y = deaths_per_1000_1to59)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  stat_cor(method = "pearson") +
  labs(x = "Distance to nearest MORDOR village (km)",
       y = "Deaths per 1000 person-years (1–59mo)",
       color = "District") +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

districts <- unique(df_all$district)

temp <- df_all %>%
  mutate(state_type = ifelse(mordorstate, "MORDOR", "non-MORDOR"))

boot_mort_state <- boot_mort_rates(
  data      = temp,
  districts = NA,
  n_boot    = 100,
  mc_cores  = avail_thr,
  group_var = "state_type"
)

boot_mort_state_df <- purrr::map_dfr(boot_mort_state, identity, .id = "replicate") %>%
      group_by(district, state_type) %>%
      summarise(
        MortRate_mean    = mean(MortRate, na.rm = TRUE),
        MortRate_CI_low  = quantile(MortRate, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE),
        MortRate_CI_high = quantile(MortRate, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
